transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood CSM), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Sophie Alvarez (Elmwood Head of ML), Mark D'Souza (Elmwood Platform Eng), Liam O'Neill (Elmwood CTO), Rachel Kim (Elmwood PM)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. quick roll call?
[00:12] Sophie: hi Sophie here.
[00:15] Mark: Mark on infra.
[00:18] Liam: Liam, CTO.
[00:20] Rachel: Rachel, product.
[00:23] Maya: Maya, cs.
[00:25] Ethan: Ethan, solutions eng. i'll do most of the technical walk.

[02:10] Jordan: goal for today is a handoff and alignment on the integration runbook, networking path for private deployment, staging access, and final pilot window. we want clear owners and next steps.

[04:05] Ethan: i'll share my screen in a sec — sorry audio hiccup — okay, runbook outline first. section one is auth and networking, section two is model routing and pinned versions, section three is observability/tracing and error handling, section four is cost controls and batching suggestions.

[05:40] Sophie: quick clarifying q: we plan to do a private deployment inside our VPC, yes? or is this dedicated hosted?
[05:51] Maya: yeah customer's asked for private; earlier conversations indicated Elmwood wants VPC peering to a Redwood private control-plane and nodes in a customer-managed subnet.

[06:30] Mark: can you run through the peering approach? last time the diagram we had was a little fuzzy about NAT and egress.

[07:00] Ethan: sure — high level: two options. 1) VPC peering with restricted routes, keep data plane in your subnet and control-plane endpoints over peering; 2) transit via a proxy in a shared VPC if you need cross-region. for most folks we recommend option 1. note: we do need specific CIDR ranges and firewall ports (443, health and metrics ports) to be opened. we'll add the exact list to the runbook.

[09:10] Mark: got it, do you support private IP-only for the nodes?
[09:18] Ethan: yes, nodes can be private. you can terminate egress through your NAT gateway. just watch the KV cache traffic — sometimes that manifests as increased outbound.

[11:00] Liam: security is a big one for us — SOC2 requirements and key management. what's the story for KMS/HSM integration and audit logs?
[11:12] Maya: we do have enterprise private with KMS integration. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS for secrets and encryption-at-rest, and we export audit logs to your SIEM. i'll attach the SOC 2 and compliance pack after the call.

[12:05] Sophie: can you confirm data residency? our product team wants tokens to never leave region eu-west.
[12:15] Ethan: yes we can pin region, but note two caveats: model catalog availability by region (some larger models might not be in all regions) and latency implications. we'll surface compatible model variants in the runbook.

[14:20] Rachel: for the pilot we'll start with the transformer-based reranker and a smaller gen model for summarization. what metrics should we give you to validate quality?

[14:35] Jordan: good question — typical success criteria are latency p95 under 450ms for short responses, error rate under 1%, and an eval pass rate on the prompt set >85% per your rubric. Sophie — you'll share the prompt set and rubric?

[15:05] Sophie: yes we'll put that together, though some prompts are messy, so expect iterations.

[17:00] Ethan: on instrumentation: we support distributed traces, token-level cost breakdowns, and per-route dashboards. we'll provide a Kibana/Prometheus exporter example in the runbook. small note — sometimes trace IDs can be mangled by internal proxies; watch for that in early tests.

[19:40] Mark: network firewall — is there a single IP block we can allow, or is it a range that changes?
[19:55] Ethan: it's a set of ranges. we'll provide static prefixes for the control plane and a swappable set for data plane; if you need static single IPs we can provision NATed egress but that requires extra config and may change cost.

[22:10] Liam: what's the rollback story if we see a regression post-cutover?
[22:20] Maya: we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to hosted model variants. CS will monitor evals and if quality drops we have an automated rollback policy. also runbooks include manual steps to switch model aliases back.

[24:00] Rachel: about observability, we need alerting thresholds. what does Redwood recommend for early warning signals?
[24:12] Ethan: p50/p95 latency delta >30% vs baseline, error rate >0.5% sustained for 5 minutes, increase in token cost >20% vs expected. we'll ship default alert thresholds.

[26:35] Sophie: can we talk about credentials for staging? how do we provision API keys and restrict them?
[26:45] Ethan: we'll create environment-scoped service tokens with limited scopes and TTLs. recommend short lived keys for staging and use SSO for prod. we can also integrate with your HashiVault if you prefer.

[29:10] Mark: curious about autoscaling behavior under burst loads. our retail endpoints can spike during promos.
[29:22] Jordan: for Dedicated/Private we expose autoscale policies — you can set min/max nodes and a burst pool. Redwood's continuous batching helps smooth token-level costs but you may need a higher min if you care about sub-200ms latency during spikes.

[31:50] Sophie: i remember earlier there was mention of quantization for cost wins. what's the recommended approach?
[31:58] Ethan: yes — for the pilot we suggest a mixed strategy: quantized smaller models for low-cost tasks and float/FP16 for high-quality reranking. we'll include recommended quantization profiles per model in the runbook.

[34:15] Rachel: timeline discussion — we want a staging pilot next week if possible. is that realistic?
[34:25] Maya: depends on a few things: runbook signoff, staging credentials provisioned, and VPC allowlist. if those land this week we can spin staging in 48–72 hours.

[35:10] Liam: our infra team needs to review the IaC snippets. can you provide Terraform examples?
[35:18] Ethan: yes we'll include Terraform and CloudFormation examples and a minimal kubernetes manifest for the edge agent.

[36:50] Jordan: ok let's capture next steps — Ethan will publish runbook with networking diagram, IaC, observability examples; Maya will send SOC2/compliance pack; Mark will provide staging CIDR; Sophie will share prompt set.

[38:40] Mark: small Q about logging retention — logs with PII? we need to ensure any partial PII is redacted.
[38:50] Maya: Redwood supports configurable retention and PII redaction hooks; for Private we can disable log retention or push logs only to your SIEM. we'll detail the options.

[40:30] Sophie: ok good. curious — any hidden costs we should watch for? egress? premium models?
[40:40] Jordan: major levers are token throughput (per-token cost), egress if you transfer out of region, and reserved capacity vs burst pricing. we'll include a cost estimate section in the runbook and an example bill of materials for the pilot.

[42:55] Rachel: who is our primary support contact during the pilot window?
[43:00] Maya: I'll be primary CSM contact for ops and Jordan for commercial. Ethan will be the SE for technical escalations; we'll provide a pager rotation if you want 24/7 during promos.

[44:30] Sophie: can we get a short checklist for go/no-go criteria?
[44:40] Ethan: yes checklist will include: network connectivity verified, service tokens issued, sample prompts pass quality threshold, tracing/logging validated, and autoscale policy attached.

[46:10] Jordan: any blockers from the Elmwood side?
[46:15] Mark: need to get security sign-off for peering; that'll take a day or two but nothing major.
[46:22] Sophie: prompt set is a bit messy but we'll prioritize a representative subset to test.

[48:05] Rachel: ok i'd like a short doc for product to explain the flow end-to-end for stakeholders — can you do that?
[48:12] Maya: yes we'll produce a one-pager and an onboarding slide deck.

[50:00] Jordan: recap of owners and dates — Ethan runbook by 2026-09-10, Mark staging CIDR by 2026-09-13, Maya schedule networking deep-dive by 2026-09-09, Sophie prompt set by 2026-09-12. pilot window target 2026-09-20.

[51:30] Liam: sounds good, let's reconvene after the networking deep-dive.

[52:05] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and links to the runbook draft.
[53:00] Maya: i'll upload the compliance pack and SOC 2 excerpts.

[53:30] Sophie: thanks all, speak soon.
[53:40] End of recording.
